in_text_mentions: controversial, and the clinical significance of pneumatosis as a solitary radiological finding remains uncertain. Nuzzo et al. [15] estimate that only 5% of patients with transmural necrosis present with wall pneumatosis at CT; other studies show that patients with wall pneumatosis showed viable intestines following surgery [47,48]. In another large multicenter retrospective study, 60% of patients were found to have benign conditions [49]. Isolated pneumatosis without gas in the portal venous system is estimated to be associated with reversible lesions in more than 40% of patients (Figure 4).

in_text_mentions: In the venous phase, the bowel walls often exhibit thickening with a multilayered appearance and reduced enhancement (“target sign”) [58]. in_text_mentions: Diagnosis of bowel obstruction led to an emergency exploratory laparotomy that revealed ascites and extensive small bowel necrosis, 50 cm upstream of the ileocecal valve, compromising the terminal ileum (Figure 2). Unfortunately, with his immunodeficient state, the devastating sepsis culminated in the patient’s death. No genetic tests were performed.

panels.rationale: Single direct abdominal radiograph of a newborn (postnatal 4th day) from a disease-focused case report titled 'Acute mesenteric ischemia in a newborn with COVID-19'. Caption states 'Free intraabdominal air on direct abdominal X-ray', and the film shows a distended abdomen with diffusely dilated gas-filled bowel loops plus free intraperitoneal gas, the manifestation that prompted urgent laparotomy for ischemic/necrotic bowel in this patient. Free intraabdominal air (pneumoperitoneum) is a nonspecific sign of perforation and is not represented in the provided vocabulary, so it is recorded as a proposed finding; bowel loop dilatation is tagged from the image. Disease attribution rests on the disease-focused article title plus this specific captioned manifestation of complicated bowel ischemia, hence moderate confidence.

plate_findings.evidence: paralytic ileus of the stomach (*) and small intestine

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is an axial CT image from a patient with acute mesenteric ischemia. Caption and in-text identify paralytic ileus and narrowing of the superior mesenteric vein (smaller SMV sign). The dilated bowel loops finding maps to the vocabulary; SMV narrowing is proposed. B: Panel B shows the same paralytic ileus and flattening of the inferior vena cava. In the context of the article's acute mesenteric ischemia case, it is included with lower confidence because IVC flattening is a supportive hypoperfusion sign rather than a specific AMI finding.
